question: How can Raman spectroscopy be used to differentiate 2A and 3T boric acid polymorphs?
answer: Raman spectroscopy can differentiate between 2A and 3T boric acid crystals based on their low-wavenumber Raman-active modes.  The 3T polymorph exhibits peaks at 111 and 201 cm⁻¹, while the 2A polymorph shows peaks at 127 and 210 cm⁻¹, differences large enough for experimental resolution.  While infrared spectroscopy is unable to distinguish between these polymorphs based on lattice modes, heat capacity measurements offer another avenue for differentiation, as the 3T polymorph exhibits significantly larger heat capacity even at low temperatures.

The purpose of the paper is to investigate the vibrational properties of the bulk boric acid polymorphs (triclinic H3BO3-2A and trigonal H3BO3-3T) using experimental spectroscopic techniques (infrared and Raman) and state-of-the-art density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
